correctness.rationale: Every row norm is t_n/(1-t_n), with sup 1/3 and sum at most 2/3. This proves boundedness, nuclearity and invertibility of I+tau A conj for 0<tau<3. The near-ball inclusions follow from inverse/direct norm estimates. For each nonzero complex functional a in ell_1, pullback has independent real-linear coordinate maps z->a_k z+tau b_k conjugate(z). Maximum-modulus attainment on the complex polydisk c0 ball forces each map to vanish beyond finitely many coordinates by the parallelogram identity. Thus a and b are eventually zero. Finite-support a has a first nonzero coordinate; strict decrease of t_n forces b_k/t_n0^k->a_n0 !=0, contradiction. These are complete infinite-dimensional arguments, not extrapolation from samples.

value.rationale: Luo resolved a long-standing failure of complex Bishop-Phelps on bounded convex sets in c0, but gave a body with a fixed square-vs-disk geometry. The new result shows that nonattainment is present in every Hausdorff and small real-nuclear-perturbation neighborhood of the canonical complex unit ball, a natural geometric stability question. The boundary is sharp qualitatively: the undeformed complex ball has coordinate modulus-support functionals, while every positive perturbation in the explicit family loses all of them. This is a substantive boundary/stability phenomenon rather than a routine rescaling or finite enumeration.
